subject: Inference performance follow-up — bottlenecks checklist & next decisions
messages:
From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
To: Alex Cheng <alex.cheng@acmeai.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Inference performance follow-up — bottlenecks checklist & next decisions

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick written recap so we have a shared checklist and next steps. I captured the items we talked through and a minimal decision path so Procurement, Engineering, and we can move toward a fast PoC.

Key pain points you highlighted:
- p95 latency spikes on short prompts (target workload: 1–3 tokens before model emits, our p95 currently ~700–900ms during bursts).
- Degraded streaming UX: partial token delivery is bursty (clients see stalls ~200–400ms intermittently).
- Concurrency/throughput ceiling on current on-prem Triton cluster (backpressure at ~18 concurrent streaming sessions for 8k-context models).
- Memory pressure on 80GB GPUs when working with 8k contexts and multi-tenant workloads.

Current stack (as mentioned):
- On-prem k8s + Triton for model serving
- Models: mix of 8k and 16k context LLMs (quantized for latency in some workloads)
- Inference pattern: a mix of short completion prompts (interactive chat) and longer batch reranking jobs in off-peak windows

Success criteria (proposal based on your needs):
- p95 generation latency < 250ms for short interactive prompts (under production-like front-end load)
- Streaming partial token arrival must be steady: token-chunk interval < 120ms for interactive flows
- Sustained concurrent interactive sessions: 50 concurrent streaming sessions on a single pool (or equivalent multi-pool routing) with <5% error rate

Suggested next steps / decision path:
1) You share a representative 1-hour traffic sample and an anonymized prompt set (we can accept a sanitized workload file). (you agreed: example_workload.json)
2) Redwood runs an initial baseline: perf capture on a hosted staging pool (we will emulate your concurrency using your sample).
3) Joint PoC scope: 72-hour canary with a Dedicated pool or hybrid routing (we'll provide an estimated config for Dedicated sizing).
4) Procurement: you loop in Procurement for standard SOW/PO timeline; we can provide a draft SOW and an estimated cost range once we size the Dedicated pool.
5) Security/compliance: we'll provide SOC2 attestation and an architecture sketch for data residency — flagged as high priority by your team.

Attachments: acme_discussion_notes_20270315.pdf (summary), example_workload.json (placeholder you can replace)

Can you confirm: a) we should prioritize p95 for short prompts as the primary success metric, and b) Procurement contact is procurement@acmeai.com so we can share a draft SOW? If yes, I’ll schedule baseline capture and propose PoC dates (we suggested Mar 24–26 for a staging run).

Thanks — short bullets are fine if that helps move things along.

—
Elliot Price
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

- Memory is a frequent limiter for us; we often fall back to smaller-context variants because the 8k runs force us to reduce batch sizes, which in turn hurts throughput.
- We also need hard clarity on data residency for inference logs — anything that touches production must stay within our MTL datacenter.

Procurement, feel free to add timeline constraints. Elliot — please include a cost range for a Dedicated pool and any VM/GPU sizing assumptions in the next note.

Hi Alex — quick tech note from our side after reading Elliot’s summary and your attachment:

Initial PoC approach (technical):
- Baseline capture: we’ll replay your sample traffic against a staging Dedicated pool with the following variants: 8k-quantized model, 8k-fp16 variant, and a 4k-context trimmed variant to measure tradeoffs.
- Streaming tuning: enable continuous batching with small max batch windows (8–16ms target) and aggressive prefix/KV cache for repeated session prompts. For chat-like short prompts we recommend prefix caching + immediate flush for first-token latency.
- Memory mitigation: explore model sharding and per-connection KV cache eviction thresholds to reduce memory pressure at the 8k context size.
- Measurement: we’ll capture per-token latencies, chunk arrival intervals, and end-to-end p95/p99 for short prompt flows.

Questions for your infra team (if you can share):
- Do you have an anonymized 1-hour traffic capture that includes both short interactive prompts and a sample of long batch reranks?
- Which GPU family is in your rack (A100 80GB, H100, other)?
- Any network egress constraints to MTL datacenter (we can design VPC peering + private routing if needed).

Short-term proposal: Provide us the sample traffic, we run a 48–72 hour baseline, then we sync on results and recommend config (Dedicated pool sizing vs hybrid routing). If you prefer, we can scope an on-prem private deployment evaluation instead of Dedicated.

I’ll prepare a short checklist and a one-page PoC SOW draft for Procurement.

—
Soojin Lee
Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
